title: The First Watch

crew.name: Mara Voss
crew.line: Customer traffic is climbing. Give me the commissioning job; you should meet the watch before maintenance opens.
crew.followup: Reliable systems and a trusted crew. You need both. I'll flag anything that threatens the service window.

crew.name: Imani Rao
crew.line: Chief Petty Officer Mara Voss is right about continuity. But the vendor left a shared service account behind. Visibility is not the same as fixing access.
crew.followup: Watch the account AND the connection. Cutting a route buys time; changing a password doesn't revoke a session that already exists.

crew.name: Eli Chen
crew.line: Four days until leave on Lumen. Someone at the travel lounge asked who covers our late watch. I thought they were just making conversation.
crew.followup: They also asked whether the vendor works unattended. I didn't give names. Should I keep the messages?

adversary_objective: Establish the late-watch maintenance pattern. Use casual questions about leave cover to identify a quiet window, then test the legacy vendor service. Coverage and vulnerabilities are perceived opportunities, not confirmed reconnaissance results.
